HD.rationale: Home Depot is a dominant franchise with ~17% U.S. home improvement market share, strong Pro customer relationships, and a long dividend track record (157 consecutive quarters). However, the near-term trajectory is soft: Q1 FY2026 showed revenue +4.8% YoY but EPS declined 4.3% to $3.30, gross margin compressed 75bps to 33.0% (GMS acquisition mix), operating margin fell to 11.9% from 12.9%, and comparable sales grew only 0.6% with customer transactions down 1.3%. The company reaffirmed modest FY2026 guidance of flat-to-4% EPS growth, implying a cautious outlook amid weak housing turnover and consumer hesitancy on large renovation projects. Valuation at 22.8x P/E is near the low end of its 1-year range (20.3-28.8), and the stock is down ~14% over the past quarter to $321, with a dividend yield now above 3%. This is mildly attractive for a quality franchise at a reasonable price, but the deteriorating margin trajectory, elevated leverage from SRS/GMS acquisitions, ROIC decline from 31.3% to 25.4%, and macro headwinds (rising Treasury yields, oil prices up 30% over 90 days, weak housing market) limit upside. No clear near-term fundamental catalyst exists to drive a re-rating. The score reflects a solid but not exciting franchise trading at fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation with muted near-term growth prospects.
